=== --help
exit 0
--- stdout
usage: hub-run [-h] [--cap CAP] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--wait ID] [--complete POINT] [--schema FILE]
               ...

Run a program that needs a capability under the platform's profile

positional arguments:
  cmd

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --cap CAP          capability name (one of the registry entry's enforce.capabilities)
  --timeout TIMEOUT  seconds (default and limit: brunna.json cap_runner)
  --wait ID          reattach to a job
  --complete POINT   a model call this project declares (registry models:): prompt on stdin, JSON
                     result on stdout
  --schema FILE      with --complete: JSON schema the answer must match
--- stderr
=== not in a project
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
hub-run: run this inside a registered project folder
=== usage: no --cap
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
hub-run: usage: hub-run --cap <capability> [--timeout seconds] -- <command…>, or hub-run --wait <id>
=== usage: no command
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
hub-run: usage: hub-run --cap <capability> [--timeout seconds] -- <command…>, or hub-run --wait <id>
=== wait: unknown id
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
hub-run: no such job: nope
=== nobody picks it up
exit 125
--- stdout
--- stderr
hub-run: job 20261031-120000-abcdef (capability gpu); if this call is interrupted, the job keeps running: reattach with `hub-run --wait 20261031-120000-abcdef`
hub-run: the platform's run service is not running (nobody picked the request up in 30 s), so the request was withdrawn. Tell the user that brunna's cap-runner service is not running
=== queued, then done
exit 3
--- stdout
--- stderr
hub-run: queued (one job at a time per project, with a platform-wide limit)
=== timed out
exit 124

=== rejected
exit 126
--- stdout

=== lost with a reason
exit 125
--- stdout

=== lost without a reason
